subject: Exec sign-off: AtlasMed Hosted API concession request
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: exec sign-off for AtlasMed Hosted API concession (DL-2027-0053)

Hi team,

Quick summary and ask: AtlasMed (healthcare SaaS) is requesting a non-standard Hosted API usage concession — 30% off list usage rates for the first 12 months in exchange for a firm commitment. Deal details are in the attached forecast and SOW. Key numbers:
- Proposed committed billing: $150,000/mo (billed monthly) for 12 months (total commit $1.8M).
- Requested concession: 30% off standard Hosted API usage unit price for the 12-month period.
- Additional ask from AtlasMed: 90-day data retention override and a tighter SLA credit structure (they want 99.95% with significant credit).

Why they matter: AtlasMed is an anchor prospect in midwest health systems; they can open an enterprise pipeline (referrals + marketplaces). If we push them to list pricing they will pause; losing them likely means >$750k ARR loss in next 12 months.

Legal/procurement have redlined our MSA (see AtlasMed_contract_redlines.docx). Procurement is requesting the 30% concession up-front. I'm asking for exec authorization for a concession >20% (requested 30%).

Proposed guardrails if approved:
- 12-month fixed concession term (then revert to list).
- Minimum committed billing of $150k/mo (non-cancellable).
- No additional business continuity SLAs beyond standard; negotiate SLA credits down with product.
- Legal to sign final redlines (Karthik).

Attachments: SOW_v1, usage forecast, contract redlines.

Please advise if we can get a conditional exec sign-off to offer 30% or if leadership prefers a counter (e.g., 25% for 12 months). Timebox: procurement expects a final answer by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: exec sign-off for AtlasMed Hosted API concession (DL-2027-0053)

Connor —

Quick questions before we escalate:
1) What's the blended gross margin impact at the proposed 30%? ballpark figures will help deal desk.
2) Is the $150k/mo commitment firm (procurement confirmed?) or subject to a PO/termination clauses?
3) Are the AtlasMed redlines asking for any indemnity or data residency language that would be a showstopper?

If margins are under 40% we should consider a tiered concession (30% for months 1–6, 20% months 7–12) or asking for a volume-recommit.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Sr. Deal Desk Manager
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: exec sign-off for AtlasMed Hosted API concession (DL-2027-0053)

Ben — answers below.
1) Margin: at list pricing estimated gross margin for Hosted API workloads ~55%. At a 30% price concession the blended margin falls to ~38% (assuming current usage mix). If we condition on committed spend (non-cancelable for 12 months) margin improves to ~42% effective due to predictability and reduced customer acquisition cost.
2) Commitment: AtlasMed has verbally committed and legal has indicated they'll convert to a PO; procurement wants the pricing fixed in the SOW. We need to harden the commitment clause in the SOW to avoid churn.
3) Redlines: main asks are 90-day retention (we default to 30/45 depending on environment) and tougher SLA credits. They also added a clause requesting broader indemnities tied to clinical outcomes — that's a hard no from legal.

My preferred path: request conditional exec approval for 30% for first 12 months if they sign the non-cancellable $150k/mo commit and accept our limit on data retention (we push them to 60 days, not 90), and legal signs off on indemnities (no expansion). If execs push back, counter to 25% for 12 months. Procurement needs a yes/no ASAP.

Connor
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: exec sign-off for AtlasMed Hosted API concession (DL-2027-0053)

Laura / team —

I reviewed the contract redlines. Legal position:
- We cannot accept expanded indemnities or clinical-outcome exposure. Mark these as deal-breakers to the customer.
- Data retention: we can agree to 60 days with standard encryption and SOC2 controls documented; 90 days is not acceptable for the hosting profile they requested.
- SLA: we can negotiate credits but cannot accept unlimited or disproportionate credit exposure.
- Anything outside these boundaries needs explicit C-level approval (not just sales ops).

Discount approval itself is a commercial decision. If leadership approves a deeper concession the legal team will work the redlines within the stated boundaries.

I'm attaching a short redline summary in the contract doc.

-Karthik
Chief Counsel (Interim) | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: AtlasMed requests 30% Hosted API concession — exec approval needed by EOD tomorrow

Rishi —

Escalating for your review. Summary: AtlasMed is asking for 30% off Hosted API rates for 12 months in exchange for a firm $150k/mo commitment. Legal will not accept expanded indemnities and recommends counter on retention to 60 days. Deal desk has flagged margin pressure but projectable ARR upside is material (anchor customer + potential marketplace listing).

Options I recommend:
1) Conditional approval for 25% concession (12 months) provided: legal finalizes 60-day retention, commit is non-cancelable $150k/mo, and we get SOC2 evidence.
2) Full 30% approval only if you accept the increased commercial risk AND we record a confirmed executive rationale (strategic priority).

Attached: SOW, usage forecast, contract redlines, forecasted ARR scenarios. Procurement wants an answer by EOD tomorrow; Connor will execute on paperwork with legal once we have a decision.

Thoughts?

Laura Bennett
VP, Americas Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: AtlasMed requests 30% Hosted API concession — exec approval needed by EOD tomorrow

Team —

Thanks for the concise summary and the financials. I've reviewed the numbers and legal constraints. I will approve a concession that exceeds 20% with the following binding conditions:

1) Approved concession: 25% off Hosted API list usage for the first 12 months (not the full 30% requested).
2) Customer must sign a non-cancellable commitment of $150,000/month for 12 months (minimum guarantee invoiced monthly).
3) Legal sign-off required: data retention limited to 60 days, no expanded indemnities, SLA credits limited per legal recommendation.
4) SOC2 Type II evidence must be provided and verified before go-live.
5) Deal desk to capture the exec concession in the deal record (HubSpot DL-2027-0053) and mark this as a one-time strategic concession; discount will revert to list thereafter.

Connor — please relay this decision to AtlasMed procurement today and prepare the SOW with the above guardrails. Ben / Marissa please document margin impact and the post-concession revert plan in the deal file. Karthik, work with the customer on the limited redlines.

Rishi Malhotra
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference
